_comment: Rough cost of analysing 100 photographs, for the confirmation prompt.
Not billing: the provider's dashboard is the authority on money.
Re-check when a vendor changes prices; `checked` is when somebody last did.

note: usd_per_100_photos = (input_tokens_per_photo * 100 / 1e6) * usd_per_1m_input
+ ((output_tokens_per_photo + reasoning_tokens_per_photo)
* 100 / 1e6) * usd_per_1m_output
Reasoning tokens are billed as output and were missing from this formula.
That is the whole of the gap between the $2 quoted for a 362-request run
and the $5 it cost: 627,000 reasoning tokens against 109,000 of completion,
roughly 5.7 thinking tokens per answering token, none of them counted.
Measured on this archive: 362 requests over 297 photographs, 109K completion
and 627K reasoning, giving ~367 completion and ~2110 reasoning tokens per
photograph across both stages. Input stays as measured before: a Stage 3
call returned 2170 input for two frames and Stage 2 sends the same 512px
preview in groups of twelve, ~1085 + ~1000 per photograph.
The reasoning figure is what the model spends at its own default, which is
what every call did while reasoning_effort was being dropped on the way to
xAI. At --reasoning low it should be lower; this stays as the pessimistic
number until a run at low has been measured, because quoting the optimistic
one is how the last estimate came to be less than half the bill.
Honest caveat: only grok-4.6 is derived this way. The two gpt-5.6 figures
predate the formula and were order-of-magnitude estimates -- they are kept
because they are the right order and marked derived:false rather than
recomputed from token prices this project has no published source for.
